My favorite part of the game was the uninterrupted 30-minute-long make-out scene between Albert Wesker and Chris Redfield, ending in them confessing their love to each other and running off into the horizon together.

While I did enjoy the game when I first played it years ago, I can't recommend you buy it as it is now since they added Enigma Protector, which is a dubious anti-cheat program that persists on your machine, even if you uninstalled the game. There are also major concerns of Enigma potentially harboring a virus/malware in its system, which has yet to be determined to be true or false. The only reason why they added it in is because Capcom has taken an insane anti-modding stance ever since a particularly infamous eSports incident in 2023 with Street Fighter 6 and now they claim that mods of all kinds (except the officially supported ones like RE4 HD Project) are no different from cheats.
This shift into forcing what is, at best an unhelpful and intrusive anti-cheat and, at worst actual malware in an attempt to police what people can and can't do with the games they paid for years ago is unforgivable and I will not be buying any Capcom games in the foreseeable future, which is a shame as I was looking forward to Pragmata and RE9: Requiem.

[b]Hey gamers, let’s talk about Resident Evil 5, a game that may not hit the horror highs of its predecessors but still brings plenty of fun to the table. Here’s why it’s worth checking out.[/b]
[list]
[*][b]A Shift in Tone: Resident Evil 5 is where the series leaned more into action than survival horror. It’s like trading creepy haunted mansions for adrenaline-pumping action sequences – not what some fans expected, but still entertaining in its own way.[/b]

[*][b]Co-Op Action Madness: This game truly shines in co-op mode. Whether you’re playing online or with a friend on the couch, blasting through hordes of enemies with a buddy adds a whole new level of fun. It’s like surviving the apocalypse with your best friend, what’s not to love?[/b]

[*][b]Stunning Visuals (For Its Time): Resident Evil 5 was a visual treat when it launched. The vibrant African setting is a nice change from the dark, claustrophobic spaces of earlier games. From sunny savannahs to creepy caves, the environments keep you hooked.[/b]

[*][b]Gameplay Evolution: Sure, it’s more action-heavy than the classic Resident Evil games, but it’s still fun. The gunplay feels solid, and managing your limited resources adds a layer of strategy. Plus, the inventory system keeps you on your toes.[/b]

[*][b]Memorable Moments: Resident Evil 5 is packed with iconic moments, from intense boss fights to that infamous boulder-punching scene. It’s like a rollercoaster of epic moments that stick with you long after you’ve finished the game.[/b]

[*][b]Controversy Aside: The game has had its fair share of criticism, from the tonal shift to some of its design choices, but it’s still a solid action game. It’s like that movie everyone loves to nitpick but secretly enjoys.[/b]

[*][b]A Love Letter to Fans: While it’s not perfect, Resident Evil 5 throws in nods to longtime fans with returning characters and connections to the series' lore. For die-hard RE fans, it’s like a reunion with old friends, even if they’ve changed a bit.[/b]
[/list]

[b]My Verdict says Resident Evil 5 might not be the scariest entry in the franchise, but it’s a thrilling action game with a co-op experience that’s hard to beat. If you’re looking for something fun to play with a friend or you’re a fan of the series, give this one a shot. It’s got just enough Resident Evil DNA to keep you hooked!"[/b]

[h1] A great, but flawed fast paced, action-focused CO-OP experience. It's still worth playing with a friend. 7.5/10 [/h1]

Resident Evil 5 is a fun, story driven 2 player co-op game with an emphasis on action instead of horror. It utilizes Resident Evil 4's mechanical blueprint for gameplay and it's great, but there's a few negatives that drags it down.

Gameplay Pros: The gunplay is solid, offering a great variety of options to choose from each weapon class. Nearly every gun is viable and fairly balanced when compared to one another. You can also upgrade all of your weapons in the shop using the gold dropped by enemies and gains earned from selling the collectible treasures. The enemies aren't bullet spongey and they constantly drop loot when you defeat them so resources aren't very scarce. The main game features 6 chapters and the levels are paced well. There are also additional multiplayer game-modes you can experience after the main story.

Gameplay Cons: All of the boss fights and mini-boss fights are [b] GARBAGE!! [/b] Del Lago and El Gigante basically return from RE4 and you fight these bosses during turret sections. You're just holding M1 and occasionally dodging whenever the prompt to do so comes up. For other bosses, you're either blasting their glowing weak points or defeating them with some scripted QTE button mashing. The 5-2 boss is [b] BROKEN [/b] on this port of the game, and CANNOT be killed using the flamethrower the game gives you. I ended up pulling out an RPG and obliterated it after wasting over 10+ minutes. You can one shot most bosses in the game with the RPG which is great for speed-runs. The boss fights are a big downgrade from RE4 which was disappointing.

Another issue with this game is the inventory. You only have 9 slots and that's all you get. I carried 3 guns, ammo for those guns, and healing or utility items for the last 3 slots. You will run into a lot of discarding or trading situations with your friend which can hinder the action. This is a big issue early game. Later in future playthroughs, you can unlock and purchase guns with bottomless mags, so you won't have to carry ammo anymore which is great.

Story: Save the world by stopping Wesker's doomsday plan, he also aura farms a lot during combat and cutscenes. He 100% carries this game and is probably the best villain in RE. The other two villains you defeat before getting to Wesker are stereotypical, and the narrative treats them like fodder trash.

TL;DR Great action-focused, CO-OP game that is 100% worth playing with a friend. The boss fights are trash and the inventory system is small, but the game makes up for these shortcomings with late game unlocks, great main villain, and the amount of fun and laughs you will experience.

RE5 is nowhere near perfect, but I don’t think it’s a bad game in the franchise either. I actually miss this version of Chris in RE7 and RE8, and we desperately need Sheva Alomar back.

[h3]Gameplay and difficulty[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
The versus achievements are a nightmare, and Professional mode can be brutal. You basically die in one hit, and some sections are so chaotic that avoiding damage feels almost impossible.

I’d honestly recommend playing it on Normal or Veteran. The game feels much better balanced that way.

[h3]Controls might feel old now[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
If you’ve been playing the recent Resident Evil remakes, RE7, RE8, or newer RE games, the controls and camera movement might feel odd at first. This is still an older game, so don’t go in expecting modern RE gameplay.

[h3]Performance[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
Definitely a good pick during a sale. It runs very smoothly even on lower-end PCs, or basically a potato. I first ran this game on a Compaq CQ40, so yeah, it can run on almost anything.

[h3]Gold Edition improvements[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
One good thing is that they removed a lot of QTEs in the Gold Edition. God, those QTEs were bad.

[h3]Final thoughts[/h3]
[hr][/hr]
If you’re coming straight from the remakes or the newer Resident Evil games, you might end up disappointed. RE5 is more than a decade old, and it shows in some places.

Still, I had a good time with it, and I’m eagerly waiting for an RE5 Remake. Hopefully, it actually happens someday.

Me and my boyfriend played Resident Evil 5 coop where the first player controls Chris and the second player controls Sheva. We had many fun moments but also many frustrating moments. I was very unsure if I should recommend it to you or not.

Let's start with the positive things. It's a really good coop action game, one of those where you have to stay together and really cooperate. The game has many environments, cool combat music and great variety of bosses! You and your partner can tease each other with your character's voice commands. We were shouting at each other a lot and it was very entertaining.

In my short clips video you can see all the good things I was writting about. We were really having fun and laughing a lot: [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qDagJpL3tm0] Fun Times in RE5 - Clips	[/url]

And here comes all the criticism I need to share with you. The Steam PC version of Resident Evil 5 has many bugs and complicated mouse+keyboard controls. I don't like quick time events very much. But the weird combinations of buttons in RE5 are unbelievable. Sometimes A+D and sometimes F+V with very short time to react to that. I watched some gameplay on consoles and they only had to press one button on their controllers. It's even more annoying during cutscenes when you sit back, enjoy and don't expect anything.

Another unpleasant moment is when you find out that you as Sheva won't get the steam achivement for finishing a chapter if your partner's game crashes or if you decide to stop playing in the middle of a chapter, save the progress and finish later. Only Chris, the player who host the game, will get it then.

It happened to us that an important enemy with a keycard we needed spawned in an inaccessible area, I was locked in a cage and my boyfriend spent quite long time trying to get there while I was waiting and waiting for ages. We tried it again and this time we only saw his shadow on the floor. I tried to use explosives so we got him down from that unknown place this time and luckily it was on the right side.

Another very annoying moment was the final boss fight where you have to press F as Sheva for almost a minute. Not just that but you have to do it SUPER fast. You kind of need to be like The Flash! I played this game 6 years ago as well and I remember I had to give up back then. It was not possible. On my last playthrough I tried it so many times and I managed to do it only once.. My finger really hurt, so I had to ignore the pain and was lucky my boyfriend didn't mess it up after that so we could continue. Uffff! These moments definitely made us want to ragequit..

RE5 Bosses in general can be very annoying. When you are not doing the right thing - shooting the right spots at the right moments , you are basically wasting your ammo and the game won't give you any more and it won't make you fail either even when you clearly can't do it. You just have to decide for yourself to restart from the last checkpoint.. But in case you somehow manage to do it but you already wasted all your ammo before, good luck to you, because you can't buy ammo directly. However you can buy weapons and sell them so you keep the ammo they had.

Final verdict: Partly recommended! Overall I am very hesitant in case of Resident Evil 5. I am a fan of RE games. I like the coop option of it. But all the bugs are breaking the full enjoyment of it for me. I believe the console version is much better! If you love Resident Evil games and you have the patience to deal with it, go for it! Wait for a sale, please. Don't pay the full price for something what couldn't have bugs fixed since 2009.

Thank you for reading my review! In case you have some questions feel welcome to ask me :)

An older entry in the Resident Evil series but non the less extremely worthy.   Even on the lowest difficulty can at times provide a challenge.  Copious amounts of lore and another stellar story in the series.  QTE sequences come out of nowhere and can result in instant death if you're not paying attention.  Once again, great weaponry, upgrades and a good selection of load-outs.  I thought the A.I. was very good and provided a great coop experience to single player.

I had significant issues playing with a mouse.  I found that the game's engine, whether purposely or not, could not keep up with high speed turning.  I used a controller which the game originally intended being a console port.

Despite the latest version ported to steamworks I had trouble launching the game which for some reason tried to launch GFWL.  Even if you don't have this issue I would recommend this guide containing QOL fixes.  https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1533171339  The guide includes an FOV fix but the FOV is still awful and something you ultimately may not be able to tolerate.  The GFWL version is available from the game's beta tab.  You can find the password in the forums.  The older more functional FOV fixes will only work on that version.

Artificial turn speed is built into the game and it's slow.  Many of the set pieces and overall game-play require usage of the quick turn function down+A.

It's not clear for first time players,  put your weapons in inventory slots up, down, left and right.  They will then be accessible from the d-pad.  Another oddity is that in the Organize screen there is an inventory move function but no inventory move function appears while in game however you can drag items around with your mouse even if using a controller.

Scaled to 4K with Lossless Scaling.  I turned down the color saturation for an awesome effect.  Combined with 4K the new veneer gave the game a great look.  Another great entry in the series.  Capcom's reputation is well earned.

Resident Evil 5 ended up being the best game I've played all year, largely because of how it completely transformed from what was supposed to be survival horror, into a co-op comedy experience from start to finish. I genuinely spent more time laughing at this game than playing it—not at any one thing in particular, but at the constant accumulation of absurd moments that kept building on each other.

A big part of that came down to my friend's outfit. I don't even think I can properly explain it, but the fact they insisted on running around in [i]that[/i] look made every single cutscene and encounter infinitely funnier. No matter how serious the game tried to be, the tone was instantly undercut the moment she appeared on screen, and it became impossible to take anything seriously after. And then there were the moments that completely broke us both: Me deciding to bring a sniper rifle into a cave and immediately becoming useless. My friend constantly reframing everything mid-cutscene—like "Chris' now facing a tough decision, between blondie and brunette", Wesker turning into a running joke as Zeno, the overly dramatic "I have a very long gun because I'm compensating for something" antagonist, especially funny because of his attempted cosplay of Neo from the Matrix.

Heck, even the most basic of interactions turned into pure comedy—I opened a door straight into an enemy holding an RPG, panicked, sprinted into him, and the rocket detonated instantly—less "take a bullet for you", more "take a rocket for you"? xD And the "Vulcan Raven" minigun boss fights had us in stitches, TWICE! Chris uppercutting a literal fucking boulder? Ahaha, it will never stop being funny no matter how many times I think about it.

That energy carried through everything—set pieces, boss fights, even basic traversal mechanics. There were so many moments where I genuinely had to put the controller down because I was laughing too much to continue playing. This is still, to this day, the best co-op experience I've ever had in a complete game. Over 1,000 hours on the 360 version, and somewhere close to that between Steam, GFWL, and retail PC disc versions of this game, I'm still enjoying every minute this game is running on any system.

But the important thing to add here is that finally, after about 5 years, the long-awaited Gold Edition content has made its way to PC (and GFWL has been replaced with Steamworks integration). Lost in Nightmares, Desperate Escape, Mercenaries Reunion, Versus, and most importantly, Warrior Chris / Heavy Metal Chris, all in 60fps here on the PC version.

A giant majority of my total hours spent in this game have been in the extra game mode, Mercenaries and Mercenaries Reunion; this is a unique time attack mode where you aim to kill a set number of enemies, breaking time bonuses and getting melee kills for additional time as you progress to complete the stage. With 18 characters / costumes across both Mercenaries and Mercenaries Reunion, as well as three variations of each of the 8 stages (Merc, Reunion, and No Mercy), there is plenty of content to keep you playing and having a good time, single player. But throw that all in with the option to play Duo for these modes (as well as the game's feature co-op campaign), and you've added hundreds of hours of additional gameplay with a co-op partner.

Lost in Nightmares, one of the Gold Edition campaigns which takes place in the flashback sequence where Chris loses his partner Jill Valentine, is one of the many highlights of the game. Like a love letter to their fans, Lost in Nightmares includes a handful of throwbacks and references to old-school Resident Evil flare (cranks, traps, a piano, and an easter egg featuring classic fixed-camera angles for the beginning segment of the campaign, to name a few). It makes me hopeful for the future of the Resident Evil franchise, and it's the most enjoyable add-on content I've ever played.

[b]RE4 with less variety, a bigger, slower protagonist, and far too many black virus worms[/b]

I can see the trepidation with which Capcom might have planned a sequel to their instant and eternal classic -- second-guessing themselves, trying to distance the new game [i]just enough[/i] from its predecessor that it would cast its own shadow, going for a more serious tone.  What they wound up with in the end, though, is precisely this:  a [i]pretty[/i] good stop 'n' shoot zombie crowd control game with a Chris [b]Roid[/b]field so uproariously meaty that he literally blocks your TPS view on occasion; a surplus of eyerolling "that part" sections; and a shocking lack of imagination on the setpiece front.  

[i]RE5[/i] still looks great and plays pretty naturally to this day, despite its generally underwhelming nature.  Can you accept an action game that's frequently un-perfect?  Are you an RE fan?  By all means, get it and play it.  Sheva's AI is not even that shabby if you're playing by yourself -- she does a fair job of healing you and conserving ammo, and she does [i]not[/i] die easily -- so don't let the lack of a human partner stop you.  The African zombies, the core of the experience, are pretty scary and fun to take out; you can set them up for melee attacks by shooting them in many more places than just the head this time, too.  The inclusion of a wider variety of gun-toting zombies (instead of just the "you-don't-have-a-gun!" heavyweight) actually adds, at times, a sense of being more intensely [i]opposed[/i] than in RE4.  The core of the action, the zombie fighting, is almost always quality stuff.

But then there's [b]that part[/b].  Or [b]parts[/b], because the game sure has its share.  Really?  Another spastic monster made of crawly black worms?  Oh, oh, Excella's test subject is getting up from the chair!  He's twitching!  He looks really scary!  He's turning into . . . [i]another[/i] mass of black worms?  *Sigh*, okay let me recharge the flamethrower, or orbital weapon, or whatever while I get [i]flopped[/i] at some more.  And who likes sluggishly dodging lasers in the (admittedly wonderful-looking) H. Rider Haggard ruins?  Getting tossed into the air over and over by lost world beams while navigating a confusing maze?  And who really derives any [i]titillation[/i] from sending this lumbering, creaking, panting mass of Redfield [i]laboriously[/i] to the many movable parts of a Zelda-style laser reflection puzzle?  Couldn't be me! 

Whereas [i]RE4[/i]'s Leon is the wisecracking action hero of eighties cinema, big Chris plays it straight -- a tortured [i]Black Hawk Down[/i] type -- so straight that it becomes its own joke.  Ever see a man punch a boulder like it's his childhood trauma?  It's almost charming really, the downright [i]autistic[/i] seriousness of Chris, but the po-faced stuff goes too far with the omission of [i]some[/i] kind of cheeky weapons salesman.  Was it too "silly" for the dev team, of all things?  How much better the game would have been, I think, if you'd been able to purchase your bullets and healing spray from a wild-eyed zombie witchdoctor wearing a necklace of finger bones, shaking a creepy skull rattle, chanting hoarsely at random intervals!

Inelegant puzzles, black worm bonanza, shaky cam seriousness . . . what else is there?  Ah, that claustrophobic [b]inventory[/b]!  Only nine little blocks for your Chris, and nine for your Sheva, with no expansions -- with you constantly running into the problem of [i]needing[/i] something that's lying on the ground in the middle of a firefight, or just really, really wanting it . . . and being unable to pick it up.  So you're constantly trying to use Sheva as your sexy packhorse until [i]she[/i] is hopelessly overburdened too, and it doesn't take long.  And then there's all these redundant weapons -- too many different weapons that do the exact same thing -- all these fully automatic bullet sprayers and sniper rifles you don't need and can't possible fit in your collection.  Hell, just shoot 'em in the elbow with the starting pistol and [b]punch[/b] to send the whole multi-ethnic horde flyin', boss!

I'm complaining more than celebrating, I know, but I promise that it's not a [i]bad[/i] game at all.  Comparisons are just too easy to make with the (still) mindblowing previous entry, and all these years later, I can't help but wonder:  [i]Why[/i] exactly did Wesker want to fill the Earth with black virus worm gestalt things?

(The included DLC is pretty okay.  [i]Lost in Nightmares[/i] gives you a classic RE mad scientist mansion and some neat atmosphere, but a rehashed, boring boss -- while [i]Desperate Escape[/i] affords a chance to pilot the lithe Jill through a challenging survival sequence where the zombies just don't stop till the timer runs down.  This is the prettiest Jill, the [b]best[/b] Jill, the most bodaciously bottom'd Jill, and it's the last time you'll ever see her.)

[b] Overview [/b]
I took far too long to finally buckle down and give Resident Evil 5 a shot. As a huge fan of the classic three, I wasn’t sure how much it would click with me as I’d often heard that it was a complete break from survival horror. Sure, I get plenty of enjoyment out of action games, but I couldn’t get hyped over what seemed like the final nail in the coffin of a series that’s always been close to my heart.

Nearly twelve years after it’s release, a friend and I decided that we’d dive into it and see what it was all about. I expected to have a good time since it was a full coop run, though I had no idea how much I was going to enjoy it. It doesn’t alleviate the disappointment of the horror being scraped away, but it does prove itself to be a solid game in its own right.

[b] Move over, Leon, Chris Is Here [/b]
It’s no secret that Leon Kennedy is my least favorite Resident Evil protagonist so it’s a personal plus to see him taken out of the role as I play through the series. Chris Redfield returns to the role and he earns a batch of action hero points for his obnoxiously swole build in this one. Seriously, he looks like he’s been surviving on a diet of steroids and protein powder while wrestling gorillas for fun since we last saw him earlier in the franchise. Over-the-top build aside, Mr. Redfield is accompanied by a new partner, Sheva Alomar, who’s quite the badass herself even though she often finds herself overshadowed by the legend that she’s with.

Like the previous entry in the series, Resident Evil 5 takes place far from Raccoon City, may it rest in peace. Our heroes find themselves investigating a biological threat that’s been making itself at home in Africa and turning the populace into nasty creatures. Both Chris and Sheva arrive as agents of the Bioterrorism Security Assessment Alliance (BSAA) and are determined to root out the cause of the recent events no matter how many obstacles may present themselves. Yes, there are a whole hell of a lot of them.

[b] Arnold Would Be Jealous [/b]
Resident Evil 5 is an action game through-and-through. It may be based on horror-like themes but it’s unlikely that you’re going to end up feeling anything resembling tension or fear. It does succeed at what it does do quite well though as the excitement kicks off immediately and you’ll find yourself in the middle of adrenaline-pumping chaos frequently.

The seeds planted by 4 have grown and matured. Currency makes its return as an important element of progression with an arsenal that steadily increases in size as you progress. Though you’ll see familiar weapons, there’s plenty of variety to be found and depending on your playstyle you may even skip or double-down on certain pieces of gear. For example, among shotguns there’s one that’s got the most bang for its buck with the highest damage per shell fired, one that’s capacity drastically reduces that amount of time that you’ll spend reloading, and another that has a wide spread meant for wiping out large groups of lesser enemies at a time. The fact that you can upgrade your weapons by their individual stats continues to be a nice bonus that keeps you invested and excited each time you loot a valuable treasure.

Kijuju and its environment still look goods good in 2021, though like the previous entry, it isn’t as soaked with atmosphere as the classic three due to its focus on combat. Many areas are clearly designed for extended, large-scale combat encounters. Enemies are everywhere, so your weapons will get a lot of use, but ammo is surprisingly plentiful so it’s rare that supply will be an issue unless you’re spray-and-praying everything that moves. Oh, and if you’re wanted to dump some of that depot’s worth of bullets, shells, and grenades into giant eyeball monsters, you’re covered here.

[b] Verdict [/b]
Resident Evil 5 is a much better game than I had expected when I had been viewing it through the lens of a Resident Evil purist. Combat is fun, the story is entertaining enough, and both of those things are made exponentially better by being able to share it with a friend in a surprisingly well-implemented full-coop campaign. Gone are the days of Leon and Ashley, Chris and Sheva make a great team and you’ll feel like you’re really counting on each other by the way the adventure is designed. You’ll even be able to laugh along at this entry’s incredibly corny villain that competes with Salazar for the ‘Villain You’ll Spend Every Encounter Rolling Your Eyes At’ award. While it may not feel like a Resident Evil title it’s an excellent shooter and one that would be a loss to miss.

Now I’m off to finally play Resident Evil 6 for the first time about eight and a half years late. Wish me luck!

[h1]Story[/h1]

After Umbrella’s apparent destruction, a mysterious company called “Tricell” takes its place. They have been conducting experiences with the locals in West Africa and the S.T.A.R.S member Chris is sent to investigate what’s going on. Along with his new partner Sheva, he will uncover a plot that menaces the whole world.

[h1]Game play[/h1]

It’s a great improvement from the game play found in RE4, here the “tank controls” are take out and a more modern “over the shoulder” shooter camera and mechanics are implemented. Still, character movement is very clunky and the characters don’t run, they just walk fast. Also jumping and taking cover are actually made through interactions with the environment. But, to be fair, the enemy movement is even clunkier than the player’s and usually enemy attacks have some kind of “wind up” movement that allows you to prevent and escape, so fair enough. 

Also, I should point that here, unlike previous Resident Evil titles, you should get enough ammo to blast through most of the enemies and situations, so it’s unlikely for you to run out of ammo in most cases.										

[h1]The Good[/h1]

This game is extremely thrilling as you are always tense to see what will come next, what enemies or monsters lie on the corner, how to solve puzzles, etc. It’s the kind of game that keeps you awake for hours in the night trying to beat a boss or solving a riddle. Some people might complain that this Resident Evil is a deviation from the series’ beginning as a “survival horror” and RE5 is more of an action game than horror. That is true, but I see it as a good thing. Here you have the chance to blast a shotgun into the face of the bad guys, unlike most boring horror games where you just run and play hide and seek with the villains. Also, did I mention how great are the boss battles in this game?

[h1]The Bad[/h1]

The game has some EXTREMELY annoying quick time events. Usually you are watching a cut scene and in the middle of it some random quick-time event appears, and if you don't press the buttons lightning fast you are insta killed! Those insta kill quick-time events are unfortunately very frequent in this game and they definitely cut down the pace and action of the game.

The game also has some bugs and issues because it was attached to the whole Games for Windows crap. Steam devs found a workaround but I still had some crashes and bugs a few times.

Also, the game has and ugly greenish gray filter all over the visuals. I guess they put it this way to look “spooky” or something. It can be easily fixed through a mod, though. Look it up

[b]Overall, this game offers a very good action/horror/whatever experience[/b]

[h1]I give it a 4.5/5.0[/h1]
